intro: Every beat you have ever nodded along to is science you can hear. A speaker cone shakes. The air passes the shake along. Your eardrum copies it, and your brain finds the pulse. In this unit you will follow that path, and you will use three of this site's instruments to do it: the Drum Machine, the Turntables and the Oscilloscope.

First you will find out what sound is: vibration, waves, pitch and loudness, and how the ear works. Then you will measure rhythm with numbers, in beats per minute and in the sixteen steps of a bar. Then you will see how people learned to keep sound, from grooves in a record to lists of numbers in a sampler. Last, you will design a beat for a purpose and test it like a scientist.

By the end, you will be able to explain why a kick drum sounds low and a hi-hat sounds high, what a DJ is really doing when they scratch, why a 1987 drum machine sounds gritty, and how to show with evidence that your own beat does what you planned.
bigQuestion: How do vibrations, patterns in time and stored waves come together to make the music we hear and create?

timeline.t: Robert Boyle hears a watch grow faint as he pumps the air out of a jar
Ernst Chladni makes sand patterns on vibrating plates, showing sound's shapes
Johann Maelzel patents the metronome, a machine that keeps a steady tempo
Scott de Martinville's phonautograph traces a singer's voice on paper
Thomas Edison records and plays back a voice on tinfoil
Amos Dolbear shows that crickets chirp faster when it is warmer
Long-playing records at 33 and one third rpm go on sale
Bronx block parties give rise to hip hop DJing
Grand Wizzard Theodore helps turn scratching into a technique
Chicago DJs build house music on drum machines at clubs like the Warehouse
The compact disc brings digital sound, 44,100 samples a second, to homes
A 12-bit, 26.04 kHz sampling drum machine shapes the sound of hip hop

test.q: Why is there no sound in outer space?
choices: There is no medium to carry the pushes
test.why: Sound needs particles to travel through.

test.q: A guitar string vibrates 880 times a second. What is its frequency?
test.why: Vibrations per second are measured in hertz.

test.q: Which change makes a sound louder but not higher?
test.why: Amplitude sets loudness; frequency sets pitch.

test.q: Which part of the ear turns vibrations into nerve signals?
test.why: Hair cells in the cochlea send signals to the brain.

test.q: By the 3 dB rule, if 85 dB is safe for 8 hours, how long is 91 dB safe?
test.why: 85 to 88 halves it to 4 hours; 88 to 91 halves it again to 2.

test.q: What is the tempo if you count 25 beats in 15 seconds?
On a 16-step machine, which steps fall on the four main beats?
test.why: Four steps per beat puts the beats on 1, 5, 9 and 13.

choices: Plays every second step a little late

test.q: A click repeats 150 times a second. What do you hear?
test.why: Repeats faster than about 20 per second blend into pitch.

test.q: What holds the sound on a vinyl record?
test.why: The groove's wiggles copy the wave.

test.q: A 33 rpm record plays at 45 rpm. What do you hear?
test.why: Faster playback raises pitch and tempo together.

test.q: Why did the 1987 sampler cut off the sparkle of cymbals?
choices: Its 26.04 kHz rate could only store up to about 13 kHz
test.why: The highest storable frequency is about half the sample rate.

test.q: You change only a beat's tempo and measure listeners' calm. What must stay the same?
choices: Nothing needs to stay the same
test.why: Controlled variables stay the same for a fair test.

test.q: Kicks on the main beats are 0.75 seconds apart. What is the tempo?

write.prompt: Claim: which sound is lower, a kick drum or a hi-hat, and why? Use evidence from sound waves, the Oscilloscope and the Drum Machine, and explain your reasoning with frequency and amplitude.
tips: Start with a one-sentence claim that answers the question.
Use at least two pieces of evidence: what the waveform looks like and what you hear.
Explain with the words frequency and amplitude.
Say how the 1987 sampler's sample rate might change the hi-hat more than the kick.
Name one thing you are not sure about and how you could test it.
